slides.headline: The rougarou was never about the monster.
Part man. Part wolf.
slides.body: From French loup-garou, werewolf. Said to prowl the swamps and cane fields of south Louisiana at night.

slides.headline: Break your Lenten fast seven years running?
slides.body: One widespread version says you become one.

slides.headline: A scary story to keep kids close to home.
slides.body: Told by Cajun families for generations.

slides.headline: Now look at what was really out there.
Real gators. Real snakes.
slides.body: Plus marsh that disorients anyone. No monster required.

slides.headline: Three centuries of retelling.
slides.body: French tales carried by Acadian and Creole families, then rooted in Louisiana cane fields and cypress.

slides.headline: The story was doing real work under the scare.
slides.body: A moral warning wrapped around a practical one.

slides.headline: Most grew up hearing a version.
slides.body: We won't say it's real. We won't say it's nothing.

slides.headline: Ask on a late-afternoon paddle.
slides.body: Manchac Mystic Kayak Tour. Small groups, real stories, told straight.
